free_tier.stated: Free, self-hosted, no storage quota: 'There is no cost to use Sonatype Nexus Repository Community Edition'; the feature matrix marks 'Unlimited Nexus Repository Deployments' as included. Storage is your blob store, so the ceiling is your disk.

egress.terms: Free by construction (self-hosted). Serve through Cloudflare or your own CDN at your own cost.

interface_detail: rest (Nexus REST API v1), native protocols for maven/npm/pypi/nuget/docker/raw/helm/apt/yum, WebDAV-ish raw repos
tooling: `curl -u` against `/service/rest/v1/components`, `mvn deploy`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`, `docker push`; a well-documented REST API for scripting.
chaining: Same as any self-hosted manager: unlimited instances × your disk. The version that matters for this brief is that nothing in Nexus meters bytes, so a single instance on a cheap VPS with a big volume gives unbounded logical storage — but you buy the volume.
limits_note: No published byte limit, but Sonatype positions CE as 'a small team solution ... with modest usage' and tells larger users to buy Pro. Pro-only features include cloud blob stores (S3/Azure/GCS), so CE is stuck on local disk. Raw repositories can hold arbitrary files but there is no public anonymous sharing story as clean as Cloudsmith's.

identity_cost.detail: derived from the record's prose, not from an identity field, and no signup was executed: epositories can hold arbitrary files but there is no public anonymous sharing story as clean as Cloudsmith's. registry

reliability_note: Mature and stable; the only 'limit' is a licensing/positioning nudge, not a technical cut-off. Data does not vanish.
